heading: SVX2 FastROM Animated Video
lede: Two complete Artemis videos: 600 frames of NASA SVS launch-and-return animation followed by 300 frames of real launch-camera footage, sustained at a verified 60 SVX2 packets/s by a 4 MiB Fast HiROM.
keysHtml: Start pauses/resumes; A resumes; L/R step one frame; Left/Right seek one second or shuttle at 2×/4×/8× when held. Keyboard and touch use the matching on-screen SNES controls.
doc:
Two videos, one cartridge

Frames 0–599 are NASA SVS Artemis animation; frames 600–899 are real launch-camera footage. Boot and random access retain independent keyframes, while sequential playback uses ordinary deltas across the cut plus a dedicated frame-899-to-frame-0 loop delta, so a slow keyframe never enters the real-time path.

Transport

Start pauses/resumes, A resumes after seeking, L/R step one frame, and Left/Right seek one second or shuttle at 2×, 4×, then 8× when held. The transport appears while paused, stepping, seeking, or shuttling. Browser keyboards and phone touch controllers use the same labeled SNES buttons.

Cartridge-native dashboard

Mode 7 video occupies scanlines 0–191; Mode 1 BG3 renders TIME, measured FPS, health, and transport below. Palette switching at the video cut preserves the dashboard colors and HDMA split.

60-packet/s full-pipeline result

The regression records 3,819 exact presentations in 3,819 eligible intervals of a 4,000-frame run, with zero decoder errors and zero deadline slips. Separate animation and real-camera screenshot rendezvous gates verify video, dashboard, palette transition, and frame order. The current masters contain distinct frames authored at 30 fps, so this cartridge is an honest 60-packet/s throughput proof that plays their motion at twice the authored rate—not yet a claim of native 60 fps source capture.

ROM SHA-256 d1b7b37aba4f28d546a63337a7f2c7d5c9d717dca3586ab6cfab4a7c5b1e70ff. Sources: NASA SVS 14191 animation and NASA Artemis I press-site camera footage. No Duck and Cover footage is present.
